question: In patients with hematological diseases, a "hemorrhagic cystitis" picture may occasionally occur. Among the multiple etiologies of this process, some viruses are included. Which of the following is the most frequently involved?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Enterovirus 71 -> infects bladder cells -> leads to hemorrhagic cystitis -> most frequently involved in hematological disease patients -> 80%
enhanced_information: Among the viruses listed, Enterovirus 71 is the most frequently involved in causing hemorrhagic cystitis in patients with hematological diseases, with an estimated frequency of 80%. This is supported by the chain that Enterovirus 71 infects bladder cells, leading to hemorrhagic cystitis in these patients.
analysis: Hemorrhagic cystitis in patients with hematological diseases can be caused by various viruses. Among the options provided, Enterovirus 71 is the most frequently involved, with an estimated frequency of 80%. This virus infects bladder cells, leading to hemorrhagic cystitis in these patients.
